title: Ashaveri Verification Policy (v1)
description: A client's pinning policy as a document: the issuers, instances, signing keys, measurements, time-source bound and vendor roots a verifier will accept, in the form a customer can read, diff, sign and hand to an auditor. The shape is strict in both directions on purpose. Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types and malformed hex or base64url are refusals, because a reader that dropped a field the operator wrote would publish a digest for a policy that is not the one they think they pinned. The digest is over the loaded document, canonically re-encoded: sorted object keys, pin lists sorted and deduplicated, and the normalised defaults written out. Reformatting a file therefore cannot change its identity. Fields that are normalised: every object's key order; the order of issuers, instances, measurements and anchor entries, each read as a set and deduplicated; a missing maxReceiptAgeSeconds or maxEvidenceAgeSeconds, which names no window of this document's own, leaves the verifier's shipped default for that field running, and hashes as null; a missing trustAnchors family, which means the verifier's bundled root for that vendor and hashes as null; and a backslash in an anchor path, which is read as a separator on every platform and hashed as a forward slash. Fields deliberately NOT normalised to their effective value: an unpinned trustAnchors family. The bundled roots belong to whichever @ashaveri/attest-core is installed, so substituting their digests would tie a signed document to a library version; null records that no root was pinned here. A missing or null maxTimeUncertaintySeconds is normalised the other way, by being left out of the re-encoding rather than written as null: a policy that demands no bound about where a stamp's source reads from is the policy that was always possible, and a key added to the canonical form moves the digest of every document already cited by one. minAnchorSlotsHeld is normalised on its own ground and the other way: a stated number is inside the canonical form and inside the digest, and an unstated demand is left out of the canonical form entirely rather than written as null, which is what keeps the digest of every policy written before that field existed the digest it already carried. minAnchorSlotsWeighed and attestedTextShapes take that same reading on the same grounds: a demand an operator states is inside the identity of the file stating it, and a demand nobody stated leaves the canonical form as it was. A policy that names none of issuers, instances, keys or measurements is refused, as is any of those four present but empty: an empty list would accept anything, and this document is a trust anchor. An attestedTextShapes that is present but empty is refused on the same rule, for naming a rule over no member at all.

v.description: Document version. A reader refuses a version it does not know.

issuers.description: Deployment ids the receipt's iss may carry. Read as a set.

instances.description: CVM instance ids the receipt's ins may carry. Read as a set.

keys.description: Ed25519 receipt signing keys, by the kid the receipt header carries.

measurements.description: Allowed launch measurements by environment kind. A kind is only ever a key here, so a measurement can never be offered against a kind it was not measured for.

maxReceiptAgeSeconds.description: How far the receipt's iat may sit from the verification clock, in whole seconds. null, or the field left out, names no window of this document's own, and both hash the same: a verifier running a policy read from this document applies its shipped default for the field. This version of the format has no spelling for a window that never closes, so that reading belongs to the policy object in the calling process, which the writer refuses to put into a document as null.

maxEvidenceAgeSeconds.description: How far the evidence timestamp att.ts may sit from the verification clock, in whole seconds. null, or the field left out, names no window of this document's own, and both hash the same: a verifier running a policy read from this document applies its shipped default for the field. This version of the format has no spelling for a window that never closes, so that reading belongs to the policy object in the calling process, which the writer refuses to put into a document as null.

maxTimeUncertaintySeconds.description: How far the source a stamp was read from may stand from the instant it names, demanded of a deployment rather than measured by it. A verifier refuses a stamp whose source declares an uncertainty above this, and the refusal names the source and the bound. This is not a window and it has no default: null, or the field left out, demands nothing about a stamp's source and leaves every verdict exactly as it was reached without the field. 0 is a demand and not an absence, so a source declaring zero uncertainty satisfies it while one declaring a number above zero, or declaring that nobody measured it, does not. An unmeasured source is refused rather than trusted, because a policy that asks for a bound is not answered by a claim nobody checked: null on a time source means nobody measured, which is a different sentence from a bound of zero.

minAnchorSlotsHeld.description: How many of a receipt's two anchor slots this verifier requires to state that their material was taken in and is held: 1 asks for at least one half of the pair, 2 asks for both, and a slot stating absent-at-source or not-taken-in answers neither. null, or the field left out, demands nothing of an anchor and both hash the same; the key is written into the canonical document only where a number was stated, so a policy that never made this demand keeps the digest it had. The maximum is the number of slots one anchor states, which the format owns as the member list COLLATERAL_ANCHOR_MEMBERS in packages/receipt/src/receipt.ts; test/anchor-slot-demand.test.ts holds this number to that list, because a pattern and a maximum can say the same figure while meaning two different things.

minAnchorSlotsWeighed.description: How many of a receipt's two anchor slots this verifier requires its reader to reach, and to find standing as the vendor's own signed statement covering the instant the receipt states. This is the second question about an anchor and not a stronger form of the one above: minAnchorSlotsHeld is answered by the artifact alone, while this one is answered by the material behind the digests the artifact names, so a slot stating held still owes it and a slot stating an absence can never answer it. null, or the field left out, demands nothing of an anchor's material and both hash the same; the key is written into the canonical document only where a number was stated, so a policy that never made this demand keeps the digest it had. The same maximum applies for the same reason: the format owns the number of slots one anchor states, as the member list COLLATERAL_ANCHOR_MEMBERS in packages/receipt/src/receipt.ts, and a demand above it is a posture no artifact can be written in.

attestedTextShapes.description: The shape this verifier demands of each text member a deployment authors inside a receipt, keyed by the payload's own member names. The eight keys are the whole class: every text a payload carries, as declared in packages/receipt/receipt.cddl, less v, which is the version this reader was built to parse rather than text an operator wrote. A key outside that set is refused as an unknown one, so a demand no reader can run never rides in a digest. Each value is a regular expression source that the whole value has to match, and the loader compiles it before it keeps the policy: a source that is not one, and one the empty text matches, are both refused, because either spells a demand that asks nothing of the member it is named for. null, or the field left out, demands nothing of any member and both hash the same; the key is written into the canonical document only where a map was stated, with its keys sorted, so a policy that never named a shape keeps the digest it had and two policies naming different shapes never share one. An empty object names a rule for no member at all and is refused, the way an empty pin list is. This sits beside the writer's own refusal and is not it: what a producer declines to sign is that producer's standard, and what a particular auditor accepts from any producer is decided here, in the reader.

trustAnchors.description: The vendor roots platform evidence must chain to. null, or the field left out, accepts the roots bundled with the verifier. An empty list under a family means the opposite: trust nothing in it, and refuse any evidence that claims it.

pinnedText.description: A value the verifier compares byte for byte, so nothing in it may be a character a reader cannot see. The class is exported by the loader as one string, and a test holds the two spellings against each other. Every escape is written as \uXXXX rather than \u{XXXX}, so the class stays inside the Basic Multilingual Plane and reads the same to a regex engine that compiles this pattern with or without the unicode flag.

publicKey.description: An Ed25519 public key: 32 bytes as base64url, 43 characters, no padding. The loader additionally requires this to be the canonical spelling of the bytes it decodes to, so that two documents naming one key cannot be written two ways.

anchor.description: One vendor root, externalised because a certificate is bytes rather than a value: the document names where it is and the SHA-256 of the bytes there. The policy digest covers this pair and never the raw text, so no formatting of the anchor file can move it. The loader reads the file, requires its bytes to hash to sha256, and refuses one that does not by name: a checkout that rewrites a PEM's line endings therefore changes the recorded digest and says so, rather than quietly standing in for the root that was signed. The path is read with either separator and normalised to a forward slash; it must also stay below the directory holding the policy file, which the loader enforces because a pattern cannot count segments.

path.description: Where the root is, relative to the directory holding this document.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes at path, lowercase hex.
